change: Compact native warnings and two choices: persistent per-session chat-only quarantine or bound checkpoint approval. Preserves the optional Agent Monitor backend.

packaged_live_tests.installation: Standalone immutable release-layout packages without node_modules; actual pinned OpenCode 2.0.22; no external LLM

agent_monitor.service: Actual Python Agent Monitor with isolated database/config/credentials

packaged_live_tests.interaction: Native session/form APIs and local deterministic model; visual UI clicks not automated

review.status: independent source review completed; findings fixed and regression tested
verified: Native forms display warning, tool and bounded reason, with exactly quarantine/allow choices and no custom answer.
Allow releases only the bound checkpoint; pre and post approvals remain independent.
Quarantine blocks tools and withholds late results, strips model-facing tool maps and preserves text conversation in the stub backend.
Quarantine persists across restarts and applies through verified parentID ancestry. Parallel approvals and other plugin instances cannot clear the local latch.
Other-instance quarantine cancels obsolete pending forms; local final release checks close asynchronous approval races.
Original results, errors, metadata and extension fields are replaced on refusal.
Optional Agent Monitor policies, trusted operator approval and execution permits are preserved. Incomplete permit/result observation remains fail-closed.
Strict versioned schemas reject mixed stub/monitor policies; illustrative requests and responses validate with regenerated bindings.

limits: The default classifier is still an always-deny stub; classifier unavailability fails open only outside an active quarantine.
The two native choices apply to backend=stub. Agent Monitor uses its own strict policy and trusted operator approval; native forms cannot override it.
Already-running tools can finish; post quarantine cannot undo side effects. This plugin is not an OS sandbox.
Tool removal is applied at context/generate/compaction hooks. Other plugins and actions outside local hooks are outside this enforcement guarantee; run the sensor last.
A failed quarantine write keeps the current instance blocked but cannot guarantee persistence after restart.
New independent sessions are not quarantined; descendants inherit by parentID, not by fork provenance.
Explicitly disabling the sensor or changing its state directory changes enforcement; local state is not protected from a user or external process with filesystem access.
No dedicated assistant message is inserted; exact subsequent LLM wording is not guaranteed.
Native API integration tested; no manual Desktop/TUI visual click test.
Noninteractive opencode run cancels native forms; use Desktop or interactive TUI for manual approval.
Self-load failures before hook registration cannot be enforced by the plugin.
